title: Invertible sheaves trivialize over inverse images of neighborhoods under finite morphisms
statement: Let $p:Y\to Z$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every point $z\in Z$ there exists an open neighborhood $V\subseteq Z$ of $z$ such that $M|_{p^{-1}V}\cong\mathcal O_Y|_{p^{-1}V}$ as sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y|_{p^{-1}V}$-modules.

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood U of z in Z and let X = p⁻¹(U), i : X → Y its open immersion, and L = M.restrict i. Since p is finite, X is affine. Invertibility of L follows from invertibility of pullback and the restriction-pullback comparison isomorphism. We work directly with the original finite map p when shrinking the target.

The set p⁻¹({z}) is finite by lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres. Its inverse image E under the injective open immersion i is finite. Apply lem-sfb-affine-invertible-finite-set-section to X, L and E to obtain a global section s nonvanishing at every point of E.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes to s. Obtain an open W of X equal to the nonvanishing locus. Its unique-coefficient clause says that s restricted to W is a free generator on every subopen, so the free-generator isomorphism and the equivalence with modules on the open subscheme give L.restrict W.ι ≅ O_W. Put O = i(W), an open of Y. Every y in p⁻¹({z}) lies in p⁻¹(U); viewed as a point of E, it lies in W. Thus p⁻¹({z}) is contained in O.

By the closed-map clause of lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres, p(Y minus O) is closed. Define V = Z minus p(Y minus O). If z were in this image, its preimage point would both belong and not belong to O. Thus z is in V. If y belongs to p⁻¹(V) but not to O, its image would belong to p(Y minus O), a contradiction. Therefore p⁻¹(V) is contained in O.

Let j : W → Y be the composite open immersion W.ι followed by i. The range inclusion p⁻¹(V) ⊆ O gives the lift k : p⁻¹(V) → W with k followed by j equal to the inclusion in Y. Restriction-pullback comparison and composition transport L.restrict W.ι ≅ O_W to j* M ≅ O_W. Pull this isomorphism back along k; pullback composition, the factorization identity and pullback of the unit identify it with M.restrict (p⁻¹(V)).ι ≅ O_{p⁻¹(V)}. All constructions also apply when the fibre is empty.

Step 1 (elementary): restrict to an affine U, using that def-weil-finite-integral-morphism makes the inverse image affine and the restriction finite. Step 2: the fibre is finite by clause 2 of the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres (finite_preimage_singleton), and the new node gives s nonvanishing on that fibre. Steps 4-5 (elementary): finite maps are closed, so V=U minus q(X minus W) is a neighbourhood of z with q^-1 V inside W, and restricting the isomorphism to it gives the trivialization. The new node lem-sfb-affine-invertible-finite-set-section is Properties 0F20 (properties.tex 5327-5380, tag/label checked in tags/tags) specialized to X affine and W=X, a correct weaker statement.
